audit_items.title: Does copy_trie produce a completely independent copy where modifications to one do not affect the other?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Prysm's Copy() uses a copy-on-write (COW) pattern with reference counting for field tries (stateFieldLeaves). Large arrays use MultiValue COW structures. merkleLayers are deep-copied via nested make+copy. The stateFieldLeaves map holds references that increment FieldReference ref counts; CopyAllTries creates independent copies when ref count > 1.
state_anomalies_found: stateFieldLeaves entries share FieldTrie references until CopyAllTries is called; mutations on original state after Copy() but before CopyAllTries() could affect both states if COW is not triggered — however the ref count check in all write paths prevents this

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: In Copy(), stateFieldLeaves[fldIdx] = fieldTrie assigns the same pointer to dst; only fieldTrie.FieldReference().AddRef() is called. If the original modifies a field trie before COW triggers, shared mutation is prevented only if all write paths check ref count. CopyAllTries (lines 1185-1200) correctly creates new tries when Refs() > 1. The condition is: fieldTrie.FieldReference().Refs() > 1, which is correct after AddRef() was called. No off-by-one observed.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: CopyAllTries is the defense against shared-mutation. The window between Copy() and CopyAllTries() is the only vulnerability surface. Whether this window is exploitable depends on caller patterns in the codebase. Internal-only access pattern.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The COW invariant holds: (1) AddRef() on copy ensures ref count > 1; (2) recomputeFieldTrie checks if fTrie.Empty() and calls resetFieldTrie which creates a new trie and calls MinusRef(); (3) CopyAllTries explicitly splits shared tries. The design is correct for the intended use pattern. The analogous property to copy_trie (EL) holds in Prysm's SSZ COW beacon state.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Reference counting (FieldReference.Refs() > 1 check) in CopyAllTries and recomputeFieldTrie ensures COW semantics

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The COW mechanism in Prysm's BeaconState.Copy() is correctly implemented. Reference counting guards prevent shared mutation. No vulnerability found.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: No action required. Code correctly implements COW semantics for SSZ field tries.

audit_items.summary: PROP-0016 copy independence is correctly implemented in Prysm via COW with FieldReference reference counting. Copy() calls AddRef(), and CopyAllTries()/recomputeFieldTrie() split shared tries when Refs() > 1. merkleLayers are deep-copied. No vulnerability.
